text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained 0.7% today, extending a strong two-week rally of 9.6%. The refining sector is benefiting from tight supply conditions: refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, diesel and heating oil inventories are relatively lean at 108 million barrels, and the company is operating in a world where crude trades at $130.80 per barrel globally while US domestic oil sits at $107. These elevated prices and high utilization rates boost refinery margins—the profit refiners make by converting crude into finished products.

The broader context is a tightening energy market despite recent headlines. Early last week, Saudi Arabia's pipeline damage from Houthi attacks sparked supply fears, but those worries eased when Saudi officials signaled they'd boost exports through alternative routes. Yet the actual supply cushion remains thin, keeping crude prices elevated and refineries running hot. Record diesel prices in particular are straining the transportation sector, which creates both inflationary pressure and sustained demand for refined fuels that keeps margins favorable for refiners like Marathon.
